references.text: The Lord predicts that He will harden Pharaoh's heart, so that he will not let the people go.
Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the Lord had said.
Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had said.
Pharaoh hardened his own heart and did not listen to them, just as the Lord had said.
Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had said.
Pharaoh hardened his heart again this time and would not let the people go.
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had told Moses.
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he would not let the Israelites go.
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he was unwilling to let them go.
Moses and Aaron performed all these signs before Pharaoh, but the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart.
The Lord says He will harden Pharaoh's heart so that he pursues the Israelites.
Paul quotes from Exodus about Pharaoh and explains how God hardens whom He wills.
Establishes a recurring pattern of Pharaoh's stubborn resistance across various plagues.
Connects the content of the prophecy directly to its fulfillment in action.
Explores the tension between human self-hardening and God's hardening, which lead to the same result.
Shows the ultimate consequence of Pharaoh's stubbornness: self-destruction in the Red Sea.
Illustrates how temporary relief led to further hardening and disobedience.
